body.q: How much did inKind raise in its latest financing tranche?

results.name: inKind Secures $414 Million Financing Led by Citi to Scale Restaurant Capital Platform - TipRanks.com
results.content:
inKind has closed an oversubscribed $414 million financing tranche led by Citi and Cross River, lifting its total capital raised to more than $1.2 billion and materially expanding its lending capacity to restaurants.
inKind has closed an oversubscribed $414 million financing tranche led by Citi and Cross River, lifting its total capital raised to more than $1.2 billion and materially expanding its lending capacity to restaurants.
Since 2022, inKind has expanded from roughly 1,000 to more than 8,500 restaurant partners and from about 1 million to over 5 million users, positioning its platform as one of the largest curated restaurant networks in the United States and giving it a growing proprietary data set on restaurant and guest behavior. Executives say this scale allows inKind to identify network-wide demand patterns and leverage AI-native capabilities to optimize guest acquisition and revenue timing for restaurant partners, creating a flywheel in which better restaurants attract more high-intent diners and, in turn, more institutional capital. For stakeholders, the new capital tranche enhances inKind’s ability to serve as a specialized finance and commerce infrastructure provider to an otherwise underbanked sector of the U.S.
Citi’s participation builds on its prior relationship with inKind through Citi Ventures, and CEO Johann Moonesinghe framed the deal as institutional validation of inKind’s restaurant-finance model, which blends upfront capital, demand generation, guest rewards, financial tools, and AI-driven insights to help operators grow without relying on traditional debt, dilutive equity, or discount-heavy marketing.

results.name: inKind raises $414M financing led by Citi, Cross River | Value Add Pulse
results.content:
inKind, an Austin-based restaurant commerce platform, closed an oversubscribed $414 million financing tranche led by Citi and Cross River, pushing its total capital raised past $1.2 billion.
inKind announced the close of an oversubscribed $414 million second financing tranche on August 10, led by Citi and Cross River alongside Sagard, Varadero Capital and Trinity Capital, pushing the Austin-based company's total capital raised past $1.2 billion, according to PYMNTS and a company release. inKind's pitch to restaurants is unusual: it fronts capital to independent restaurants in exchange for future dining credit, which it then sells to consumers at a discount -- functioning less like a typical venture-backed startup and more like a structured-finance vehicle wrapped in a consumer app.
The lead investors here -- Citi and Cross River -- are banks, not venture funds, which fits the nature of the raise: this is largely debt-like financing capital inKind deploys to restaurants, not equity funding a typical product roadmap. Cross River in particular has built a business as the banking-as-a-service layer behind multiple fintech platforms, and its participation alongside Citi signals inKind's model has matured into something banks are comfortable underwriting at scale rather than a venture-stage experiment -- a different investor profile than the venture-led rounds Pulse covered elsewhere this week in embedded fintech.
The $30 billion GMV figure across 8,500 restaurants implies roughly $3.5 million in average annual volume per restaurant flowing through inKind's platform, though the company hasn't disclosed what share of that volume is inKind-funded credit versus organic restaurant revenue passing through its systems. inKind competes for restaurant relationships against traditional revenue-based financing providers and card-linked offer platforms, but its dining-credit model is closer in structure to a prepaid gift-card business than to a typical restaurant-tech SaaS product -- closer to a company like Toast on distribution but fundamentally a different, credit-driven business underneath.
The company hasn't disclosed default or restaurant-closure rates within its network, information that would matter more to evaluating this raise than the topline GMV number. Watch whether inKind discloses restaurant-level default rates in future raises -- that's the number that actually tells you whether $1.2 billion in cumulative financing is building a durable credit book or accumulating risk faster than the model can absorb it.

results.name: inKind Raises $414M in Funding
results.content:
inKind, an Austin, TX-based provider of a curated restaurant commerce and growth platform, raised $414M in funding
inKind, an Austin, TX-based provider of a curated restaurant commerce and growth platform, raised $414M in a second financing tranche. The first tranche was announced at the beginning of July 2026. The round was led by Citi and Cross River with participation from Sagard, Varadero Capital, and Trinity Capital. The raise brought the total amount to more than $1.2B. The company intends to use the funds to expand operations and its development efforts.

results.content:
The transaction brings inKind's total capital raised to more than $1.2 billion. Just as Airbnb built infrastructure connecting hosts and travelers, and DoorDash built infrastructure connecting merchants and consumers, inKind is building growth ...
The new tranche significantly expands the group of institutional investors supporting inKind's growth. Together with Liberty Mutual Investments debt investment, the new financing provides inKind with additional long-term capacity to support restaurant operators nationwide and further validate the company's model as an emerging institutional asset class. inKind's selectivity is central to both its credit model and its network economics.
10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- inKind, the curated restaurant commerce platform helping great restaurants access capital, guests, and technology, today announced the closing of an oversubscribed $414 million second financing tranche led by Citi and Cross River alongside Sagard, Varadero Capital, and Trinity Capital. The transaction brings inKind's total capital raised to more than $1.2 billion. Just as Airbnb built infrastructure connecting hosts and travelers, and DoorDash built infrastructure connecting merchants and consumers, inKind is building growth infrastructure that connects restaurants with capital and high-intent guests. Its platform combines upfront capital, demand generation, financial tools, guest rewards, proprietary data, and AI-native capabilities.
It also expands the capital foundation behind a commerce platform that becomes more valuable as more restaurants and diners join and its proprietary data advantage deepens. "For more than a decade, inKind has been building a new way to finance and grow great restaurants," said Johann Moonesinghe, co-founder and CEO of inKind.
It took years of performance, discipline, and proof before institutional investors began to understand the asset class we were creating. The addition of Citi, a global systemically important bank, is an important signal that the market increasingly recognizes the strength of the inKind model. This financing gives us the capacity to scale the restaurant commerce infrastructure we have spent more than a decade building."

results.name: inKind Secures $414 Million Financing, Bringing Total Capital Raised Above $1.2 Billion
results.content:
inKind has closed an oversubscribed $414 million second financing tranche led by Citi and Cross River, bringing the restaurant commerce platform’s total capital raised to more than $1.2 billion.  
The financing includes $175 million from Citi and $150 million from Cross River at the senior level, along with $50 million from Sagard, $25 million from Varadero Capital and $14 million from Trinity Capital in mezzanine financing.  
The closing follows a recently announced $320 million commitment from Liberty Mutual Investments as a senior anchor and mezzanine lender. With the expanded facility, inKind plans to deploy more than $1 billion in growth capital to nearly 10,000 restaurants over the next year.  
Citi’s participation also expands an existing relationship with inKind, following a 2025 investment by Citi Ventures.  
inKind operates a restaurant commerce platform that combines upfront capital, demand generation, financial tools, guest rewards, proprietary data and AI-native capabilities. Its network currently connects more than 5 million diners with more than 8,500 restaurants representing nearly $30 billion in annual restaurant gross merchandise value.  
The company has expanded from approximately 1,000 restaurant partners in 2022 to more than 8,500 today. Its user base has also increased from roughly 1 million in March 2024 to more than 5 million.
inKind has provided more than $850 million in growth capital to restaurant partners and delivered more than $225 million in dining rewards to guests. Its restaurant partners include MINA Group, Ethan Stowell Restaurants, José Andrés Group, Okàn, Kann and Superiority Burger.  
**KEY QUOTES:**  
*“For more than a decade, inKind has been building a new way to finance and grow great restaurants.”*  
*“The addition of Citi, a global systemically important bank, is an important signal that the market increasingly recognizes the strength of the inKind model. This financing gives us the capacity to scale the restaurant commerce infrastructure we have spent more than a decade building.”*  
*“We believe inKind is still in the early chapters of what it can become. As our restaurant network grows, we can give more great operators access to millions of guests. As our guest base grows, we can give more diners access to the best restaurants in the country.”*  
**Johann Moonesinghe, Co-Founder and CEO of inKind**

Austin-based restaurant commerce platform inKind has secured $414 million in new financing led by Citi and Cross River, bringing its total capital raised to more than $1.2 billion as the company expands its restaurant growth platform across ...
Austin-based restaurant commerce platform inKind has secured $414 million in new financing led by Citi and Cross River, bringing its total capital raised to more than $1.2 billion as the company expands its restaurant growth platform across the United States. The oversubscribed second financing tranche includes $175 million from Citi and $150 million from Cross River in senior financing.
Today, the inKind restaurant network connects more than 5 million diners with more than 8,500 restaurants representing nearly $30 billion in annual restaurant gross merchandise value, or GMV. The $414 million financing follows a recently announced $320 million commitment from Liberty Mutual Investments, which is participating as a senior anchor and mezzanine lender. With its expanded financing capacity, inKind plans to deploy more than $1 billion in growth capital to nearly 10,000 restaurants over the next year.
Unlike traditional debt financing, which can create ongoing repayment obligations, or equity financing that can dilute an owner’s stake, inKind provides restaurants with upfront capital while also helping generate customer demand through its dining network.
The involvement of Citi, Cross River, Liberty Mutual Investments and other institutional capital providers is a sign that investors are now more open to inKind’s approach to restaurant financing. For inKind, the opportunity extends beyond providing capital. The company is positioning itself as a broader restaurant commerce infrastructure platform where growth in its restaurant network attracts more diners.

results.content:
## How Much Funding Has inKind Raised?  
inKind has successfully raised funds through 2 rounds, with the latest being a Growth Capital led by Citi. With a total of $1.2B+ raised, the company continues to expand its operations.  
Lead Investors  
Citi, Cross River  
Valuation at Round  
Not publicly disclosed  
Motivation Behind the Round  
inKind raised $414 million in a second financing tranche to deploy over $1 billion in growth capital to nearly 10,000 restaurants over the following year, expanding both its restaurant network and its diner membership base.  
Lead Investors  
Liberty Mutual Investments  
Valuation at Round  
Not publicly disclosed  
Motivation Behind the Round  
inKind raised $320 million in a first financing tranche to expand the capital it could deploy to independent restaurants, scaling its model of providing upfront growth capital tied to future dining spend.  
Total Amount Raised: $1.2B+
## Key Investors  
Citi  
Strategic Investor  
Citi is a global financial institution and one of the largest banks in the United States. Citi provided $175 million as part of the $414 million August 2026 financing tranche, serving as co-lead alongside Cross River. Citi Ventures had previously invested in inKind before the larger capital facility commitments.  
Cross River  
Strategic Investor  
Cross River is a technology-driven financial services company and bank specializing in providing financial infrastructure to fintech companies. Cross River contributed $150 million to inKind's August 2026 financing tranche as co-lead alongside Citi.  
Liberty Mutual Investments  
Asset Manager  
Liberty Mutual Investments is the investment arm of Liberty Mutual Group, one of the largest global property and casualty insurers. Liberty Mutual Investments committed $320 million to inKind's first financing tranche in July 2026.  
Sagard  
Growth Equity  
Sagard is a multi-strategy alternative asset manager with expertise in credit and equity investments. Sagard contributed $50 million to inKind's August 2026 financing tranche.
## What's Next for inKind?  
inKind has stated plans to deploy over $1 billion in growth capital to nearly 10,000 restaurant partners over the next year, more than doubling its current network. The company is expanding its AI-native capabilities across demand generation, guest rewards, and financial tools, which will require investment in data infrastructure and engineering headcount. The oversubscribed nature of the August 2026 raise signals strong institutional confidence in inKind's repayment model and the durability of independent restaurant dining. Additional financing tranches or an equity raise to support the technology platform are plausible as the network scales.  
Prospecting window  
inKind surpassing $1.2 billion in total capital raised with plans to deploy over $1 billion to nearly 10,000 restaurants in the next year creates an active vendor evaluation window for restaurant technology, payments, loyalty, and data platforms. VP of Product, Head of Engineering, Chief Technology Officer, and VP of Data at inKind are the primary contacts for technology vendors. The company's stated expansion into AI-native capabilities signals active procurement for AI tooling, data infrastructure, and personalization platforms. The restaurant partner network of 8,500 locations is also a prospecting pool for any vendor selling into the hospitality and food service sector.
